rule: Anchors applied ONLY where the existing frozen historical evidence (already exposed to PASS A / targeted PASS A rerun) contains the required metrics. No new evidence gathered, no input manufactured. PASS A / targeted-rerun / PASS B artifacts are NOT overwritten -- this is a separate, diagnostic-only simulation.

newly_scoreable_cells.evidence: Disclosed merchant count grew from ~20,000 (2010, exact month unspecified) to over 80,000 (Dec 2013) -- a real, dated, two-point series.
newly_scoreable_cells.exact_anchor_used: Part 2 (Customer Growth), SMB SaaS/platform family: floor ~500-1,000 merchants cleared; ~4x growth over an approx. 3.5-year window read against stage-appropriate expectations for a 7-year-old company -- strong, unambiguous evidence of sustained platform demand.
newly_scoreable_cells.confidence: Medium (the series itself is High-confidence/dated at both ends; Medium reflects the imprecise 2010 start month, which affects the CAGR calculation used for the related Growth Velocity score, not the qualitative growth read itself)
newly_scoreable_cells.reason: 4x growth in a core usage-count metric, at a scale already well past the 'is this real' floor, for a company past its earliest stage, is direct and strong evidence of healthy demand growth -- exactly the evidence-status this dimension exists to capture.

newly_scoreable_cells.evidence: Same merchant-count series as Customer Growth above.
newly_scoreable_cells.exact_anchor_used: Part 1 (Growth Velocity): floor cleared; annualized CAGR = (80000/20000)^(1/3.5) - 1 ~= 48.6% (3.5-year window used as a conservative midpoint estimate given the unspecified 2010 start month -- flagged explicitly as an estimate, not a precise figure); Tier 3-4 (medium-to-large merchant-count scale) band: 40-100% CAGR = Strong. 48.6% sits near the low end of that band.
newly_scoreable_cells.confidence: Medium-Low (score depends on an estimated, not exact, measurement window -- the CAGR could reasonably range from the mid-40s to high-50s% depending on the true 2010 month, which would not change the band but does limit precision within it)
newly_scoreable_cells.reason: Distinct from Customer Growth's more literal series read: this is the rate-normalized-by-scale question, and 48.6% CAGR from an already-substantial merchant base clears the 'Strong' bar for this scale tier without reaching 'Exceptional.'

newly_scoreable_cells.evidence: 'Significant underwriting losses as the company scaled,' explicitly reported alongside the valuation increase.
newly_scoreable_cells.exact_anchor_used: Part 4, insurance/underwriting family, qualitative-fallback row: an explicit, dated, company-specific disclosure of significant losses (not generic industry commentary, not source-flagged as ambiguous) satisfies the qualitative bar even without a numeric loss ratio.
newly_scoreable_cells.confidence: Low-Medium (directionally clear and company-specific, but the magnitude of the loss is not quantified)
newly_scoreable_cells.reason: This is the one case in the Unit Economics review where a qualitative disclosure is specific and unambiguous enough to support a score under the new family definition, rather than remaining Category A/C (see Part 4/8 note below on the resulting double-count tension).
newly_scoreable_cells.IMPORTANT_CAVEAT: This evidence is the SAME underlying fact already used to score Oscar Health's Burn Efficiency=3 in the targeted PASS A rerun (which explicitly flagged the reuse risk when it was made). Scoring it again here for Unit Economics creates a real double-citation across two Financial Health dimensions. This simulation reports the result honestly rather than silently resolving it -- see Part 11 of ANCHOR_DESIGN.md. In this specific case the pillar-level numeric effect happens to be neutral (both dimensions independently land on 3), but the underlying evidence-reuse tension is real and should be resolved by a human decision (or a future evidence-attribution safeguard), not by this simulation.
